s1.syndrome_frame: Acute liver injury with cholestatic features in a patient with recent medication start
salient_findings: Generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, γ-glutamyl transferase)
key_facts: 65-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia
Prostate-specific antigen level was 0.796 ng/mL
Uroflowmetry revealed reduced urine flow, prolonged micturition time, and obstructive findings
Started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily
Symptoms started on day 9 of therapy
Denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
No history of liver disease
Jaundiced but no stigmata of chronic liver disease on examination
Leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL
Elevated liver enzymes (AST 175 U/L, ALT 402 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 235 U/L, γ-glutamyl transferase 327 U/L)
Hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL)
Normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts on abdominal ultrasonography
Negative serologic tests for viral hepatitis and autoimmune markers

shortlist.label: Drug-induced liver injury
shortlist.why_kept: Recent start of Alfuzosin and development of liver injury

shortlist.label: Primary biliary cholangitis
shortlist.why_kept: Cholestatic features and elevated alkaline phosphatase

shortlist.label: Autoimmune hepatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and negative serologic tests for viral hepatitis

shortlist.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
shortlist.why_kept: Cholestatic features and normal abdominal ultrasonography

raw.rationale: The patient started experiencing symptoms such as loss of appetite, malaise, generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice on day 9 of Alfuzosin therapy, which suggests a temporal relationship between the drug initiation and the onset of liver injury. The patient denied use of other hepatotoxic medications and had no history of liver disease, making drug-induced liver injury the most plausible explanation for the elevated liver enzymes and hyperbilirubinemia.

rejected.label: Primary biliary cholangitis
rejected.why: Negative autoimmune markers and normal liver, gallbladder, and bile ducts on ultrasonography make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Autoimmune hepatitis
rejected.why: Negative autoimmune markers and lack of other characteristic features of autoimmune hepatitis

rejected.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
rejected.why: Normal liver, gallbladder, and bile ducts on ultrasonography and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography make this diagnosis unlikely

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholestasis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase, the temporal relationship with Alfuzosin initiation and the absence of other characteristic features of intrahepatic cholestasis make drug-induced liver injury a more likely diagnosis
